title.en: Practice Questions and the Real Exam

summary.en: Hide four fruit cards and compare a broad rule, a flexible rule and an overly simple guess.
summary.bn: চারটি ফলের কার্ড লুকিয়ে মাঝারি নিয়ম, অতিরিক্ত খুঁটিনাটি নিয়ম আর খুব সাদামাটা আন্দাজ তুলনা করো।

keywords: Practice Questions and the Real Exam

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: Lock a rule before opening the envelope
What the hidden pile tells you

practice.title: Separate the piles
practice.statementHtml: For ten cards with the last four hidden, identify training and test roles.
hints: The labels in the hidden pile must not guide fitting.
practice.answerHtml: The first six cards form training. The last four form test. Training labels can select rules, while test labels are revealed only after guesses are fixed.

practice.title: Read the scores
practice.statementHtml: Explain the flexible rule’s result: zero training mistakes, two test mistakes.
hints: Name what is remembered and which new points fail.
practice.answerHtml: Every training size matches itself, so the rule memorises those labels. Hidden apples at 2.7 and 3.3 are nearest to the isolated training mango at three, causing two mistakes. The score gap warns about poor transfer.

practice.title: Too little pattern
practice.statementHtml: Explain why an always-apple rule is underfitting here, rather than a safe default with proven accuracy.
hints: Count mangoes in the training set.
practice.answerHtml: There are three training mangoes and three apples. Always apple misses all three mangoes and ignores useful size structure. It is a comparison baseline, not evidence that apple is the right answer for new fruit.

practice.title: A fair rerun
practice.statementHtml: A student chooses the flexible model after seeing hidden answers, then reports them as untouched test evidence. Propose an honest revision.
hints: Acknowledge which answers shaped the choice.
practice.answerHtml: Record that the set was used during development. Keep its result as exploratory evidence, then reserve another independent hidden set for a final check. Do not describe reused answers as untouched.

quiz.prompt: Read the mistake bars. Which rule gets every training card right but misses two hidden cards?
options: Simple
Flat
Flexible
All three
quiz.explanation: The flexible rule has a zero training bar and a test bar of two. That gap is the warning illustrated by these cards.

caption.en: Six training and four hidden cards: counts from three fitted size-only rules.
caption.bn: ছয় training, চার test কার্ডে তিন আকারভিত্তিক নিয়মের ভুল।

quiz.prompt: Read the split table. Which cards are kept out of training?
options: p1 through p6
Only p3
All ten cards
p7 through p10
quiz.explanation: The first six rows say Training. The last four say Test hidden and their answers must not guide fitting.

caption.en: The first six cards train; the last four answers stay sealed until prediction.
caption.bn: প্রথম ছয়টিতে শেখা, শেষ চারটির উত্তর অনুমানের আগে ঢাকা।

quiz.prompt: Which information may influence the trained fence before hidden labels are opened?
options: The six training measurements and labels
The four hidden correct names
A correction based on the final test mistakes
A ranking chosen after all test answers are revealed
quiz.explanation: The test answers judge a fixed model afterwards. Letting them select the fence would break the intended separation.

quiz.prompt: Why can the nearest-size rule get all six training cards right here?
options: It uses the future test answers
Each training size is its own nearest example
Every card in the world has a unique perfect name
It ignores every training label
quiz.explanation: These six sizes are distinct, so a training card has itself at zero distance. That helps memory but does not establish transfer.

quiz.prompt: Why are the hidden apples at sizes 2.7 and 3.3 called mango by the flexible rule?
options: They are physically mangoes after prediction
Their sweetness must equal their card identifiers
The training mango at size 3 is closest
The flat majority is mango
quiz.explanation: Both sizes are nearest to three, whose supplied label is mango. The fixed rule makes two errors against the hidden apple names.

quiz.prompt: Which result best illustrates underfitting in the demonstration?
options: The flexible rule uses all distinct training labels
The hidden labels stay sealed
A learner records a guess before seeing an answer
The flat rule misses three training cards by calling everything apple
quiz.explanation: The flat rule cannot use the broad size pattern. It is too restricted even on the examples available for learning.

quiz.prompt: What is overfitting in the practice-book analogy?
options: Remembering details that do not carry well to unfamiliar questions
Making any single mistaken guess
Using a model with any adjustable value
Hiding answers before a final check
quiz.explanation: The important issue is weak transfer despite strong familiar performance. A single error or a parameter alone does not define it.

quiz.prompt: Why does the flat rule select apple when training labels tie three to three?
options: The test answers secretly choose apple
The example declares apple as its tie convention
Apple is guaranteed to be the majority of future fruit
Ties must be broken by sweetness
quiz.explanation: A declared tie rule keeps the demonstration deterministic. It does not establish any universal future majority.

quiz.prompt: How should you read the training and test mistake counts when pile sizes differ?
options: Ignore pile sizes because all counts are percentages
Assume the taller bar always comes from more examples
Read each count together with its number of cards
Treat every count as a future guarantee
quiz.explanation: Three mistakes out of six and two out of four need their denominators for interpretation. These charts show counts, not percentages.

quiz.prompt: After inspecting test answers, you change the model. What is needed for a fresh final assessment?
options: The same revealed cards called hidden again
Training on all revealed answers and quoting the old score
Deleting every test error from the record
Another unseen set kept out of those changes
quiz.explanation: The revealed set has now influenced development. New evidence is needed to judge the revised model honestly.

quiz.prompt: The simple rule names all four test cards correctly. Which claim is justified?
options: It made no mistakes on these four cards
It will name every future fruit correctly
All more flexible rules are always harmful
Four successes prove every possible dataset is covered
quiz.explanation: A small successful check has a narrow scope. Broader and representative evidence is needed for stronger claims.

quiz.prompt: Why does this lesson disclose that the first cards train and the last cards test?
options: Row order can never affect a result
The ordered split is a transparent paper demonstration, not a universal splitting method
All real measurements are already randomly ordered
Ordered splits always prevent every kind of leakage
quiz.explanation: The classroom counterexample deliberately uses that order. Real tasks need a split appropriate to time, groups and future cases.

keyPoints.en: Training examples help choose a model.
Test answers stay outside that choice.
keyPoints.bn: Test উত্তর সেই বাছাইয়ের বাইরে থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Overfitting can produce a perfect practice score and weaker new guesses.
keyPoints.bn: Overfitting-এ অনুশীলনে সব ঠিক, নতুনে দুর্বল হতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Underfitting misses useful structure even on familiar examples.
keyPoints.bn: Underfitting চেনা উদাহরণেও কাজের ধরন বাদ দেয়।

keyPoints.en: Counts need pile sizes and representative cases for context.
keyPoints.bn: ভুলের সঙ্গে স্তূপের সংখ্যা ও ধরন জানতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Revising from test answers uses up their freshness.
keyPoints.bn: Test দেখে বদলালে তার অচেনা থাকার সুবিধা ফুরায়।

keyPoints.en: Four successful guesses cannot guarantee every later answer.
keyPoints.bn: চারটি ঠিক উত্তর সব ভবিষ্যৎ উত্তর নিশ্চিত করে না।

examQuestions.question: For flat, simple and flexible models, state the training and test mistakes in the ten-card demonstration.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Flat has three mistakes among six training cards and two among four test cards. Simple has one training mistake and zero test mistakes. Flexible has zero training mistakes and two test mistakes. These are counts for this specific collection.

examQuestions.question: Explain why test labels must be hidden during model choice.
examQuestions.answerHtml: If they influence the choice, the learner is being adjusted to the check itself. Hiding them preserves a separate look at unfamiliar cases after predictions are fixed.

examQuestions.question: Apply the learned size-five simple rule to test sizes 2.7, 3.3, 5.5 and 8, whose labels are apple, apple, mango and mango.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The first two sizes are below five and receive apple. The last two exceed five and receive mango. Each matches its supplied name, so there are zero test mistakes on these four.

examQuestions.question: Contrast overfitting and underfitting without saying complex models are always bad.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Underfitting happens when the rule cannot capture useful patterns even on training examples, like always apple. Overfitting follows training details that fail to transfer, like copying the isolated size-three mango. Some tasks require flexible rules; judge transfer with independent evidence rather than complexity alone.
